reason: The text explicitly demonstrates agency among non-leaders, particularly the common people (הָעַם). While Moses and Aaron are instructed leaders who receive God's commission, the text also shows the broader populace exercising agency: they believe (וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם), they listen (וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ), and they worship (וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ). These are active choices expressed through volitional verbs. Additionally, Moses himself demonstrates individual agency through his objections and negotiations with God (וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל־ יְהוָה בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָי...), showing that agency is not restricted to the formally designated leader but extends to individuals in conversation with divine authority.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
